initial_requirements: A stock trading platform needs a Central Trading System as one subsystem within a larger trading environment. It must receive trading instructions from the client-facing service, distinguish among different instruction types, and match compatible stock orders according to the applicable trading rules. The subsystem must also communicate the resulting trading information to other parts of the platform and allow authorized system managers to inspect its information.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What specific functions should the Central Trading System perform from end to end—for example, how should it receive and classify incoming trading instructions, determine whether orders can be matched, execute or record the match outcome, and publish the resulting trading information to other system components?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
From our side, it should accept trading instructions from the client-facing service, validate that they’re complete and authorized, and then classify them into the right order type, like buy, sell, amend, or cancel. After that, it should apply the trading rules to see whether compatible orders can be matched, and if they can, carry out the match and record the result; if not, it should leave the order open or reject it depending on the instruction and rule outcome.
Once the decision is made, it should publish the trading outcome to the rest of the platform, including the executed trade details, any partial fill information, or a clear rejection or cancellation status. It also needs to keep its own records so authorized managers can inspect what happened later.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Build a Central Trading System that accepts trading instructions, applies trading rules to match orders, records trading outcomes, publishes results to other platform components, and supports manager inspection.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Client-facing service as the source of trading instructions; authorized system managers as users who inspect system records; other platform components that receive published trading outcomes.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Receive trading instructions from the client-facing service; validate completeness and authorization; classify instructions as buy, sell, amend, or cancel; apply trading rules to determine match compatibility; execute matches and record results; keep orders open or reject them when appropriate; publish executed trade details, partial fill information, rejection status, or cancellation status; maintain internal records for later inspection.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: Trading instructions must be complete and authorized before processing; orders must be classified into valid instruction types; matching must follow applicable trading rules; compatible orders may be matched, otherwise the order is left open or rejected based on the instruction and rule outcome; partial fills and cancellations must be represented in the outcome.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Trading instructions, order types, stock orders, matched trades, executed trade details, partial fill information, rejection status, cancellation status, internal trading records.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Only authorized instructions may be processed; the system operates as a subsystem within a larger trading platform and must publish outcomes to other components; authorized managers must be able to inspect stored information.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Accuracy of validation, classification, matching, and status reporting; traceability through retained records; reliable publication of trading outcomes for downstream components.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: If an instruction is incomplete or unauthorized, it should not be processed normally; if no compatible match is found, the order should remain open or be rejected depending on the instruction and rule outcome; outcomes may be executed trade, partial fill, rejection, or cancellation.
